A black and white luxury fashion campaign photograph made in a black photo studio: She walks slowly across the black studio in the ivory satin slip and cardigan, our bag hanging from her hand at her side.

References: Image 1 is THE SHOPPING BAG: our matte warm ivory bag with flat espresso ribbon handles; take its exact proportions, folded cuff and handles. Image 2 is THE WOMAN (character 13): about 28, Irish, fair freckled skin, straight auburn shoulder-length hair, slim build, slim freckled hands. Face not shown. Use only the face, hair, skin, hands and build from this sheet; ignore the clothes in it. Image 3 is THE OUTFIT: take exactly this ankle-length ivory satin slip dress with the cowl neckline and the oversized ivory knit cardigan draped over the shoulders, ivory pointed mules. The output is one single photograph, portrait 4:5.

Shot: Camera at hip height, 50mm lens, f/2.8, side on to her. The frame is cropped from just below her shoulder to her knee; the bag hangs on the right half of the frame by its ribbon handles from her relaxed hand, the bag front square to the camera, filling about 45 percent of the frame width, sharp. One large soft light from the left, like a tall window, wraps the satin and the bag and falls off into pure black on the right. Only her body from just below the shoulder to the knee and her hand are in frame, side on, in exactly the outfit from the reference. Her face is never visible: she is turned away or cropped by the frame, and no face, cheek, chin or profile shows.

Place: A black photo studio: a matte black backdrop and a dark floor, nothing else unless the shot names it.

Light: One real light source exactly as the shot describes; deep true blacks around it, no fill, nothing evenly lit.

Palette and grade: Black and white photograph: deep true blacks, soft graded greys, clean paper whites; no colour at all. The design surface is the cleanest white in the frame.

Real: this is a product mockup photograph for a fashion campaign, so the design surface is the hero: it stays sharp, clean and fully readable inside the effect, never covered by it. It is a real photograph made in camera by a campaign photographer, not a render and not a digital filter. The design surface faces the camera almost square-on, within about 15 degrees, so it reads flat and undistorted; its four edges run parallel to the edges of the photograph, a true rectangle, never a trapezoid or keystone; flat things on a table are shot from nearly straight above. Only the objects named in the shot are on set. The design surface is new and clean, crisp at its edges and corners, without blowing out.

Design surface: THE BAG FRONT IS PLAIN MATTE PAPER-WHITE BOARD, flat with crisp folded edges and a deep folded top cuff, nothing printed on it.

Finish: Shot on 35mm Kodak Tri-X at box speed, developed in D-76 and printed on fibre paper: fine but clearly visible film grain, rich blacks, smooth tonal roll-off in the highlights, tiny real imperfections of film. Calm, quiet and physical, like a printed campaign; never smooth, never glossy, never a digital render.
